newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian prosecutors arrest former bank chairman.
newsitem.headline: Romanian prosecutors arrest former bank chairman.

text.p: The former head of Romania's leading state-run bank, Bancorex, was charged with embezzlement on Wednesday, his lawyer said.

Razvan Temesan, in police detention since Tuesday, is alleged by prosecutors to have used his position between 1992 and earlier this year to offer a string of companies and individuals the use of luxury cars belonging to the bank.

Temesan is the latest of several prominent entrepreneurs to be investigated for corruption since reformist president Emil Constantinescu defeated an ex-communist in last November's election. Constantinescu made the fight against corruption a priority in a bid to lift Romania's sagging economy.

The prosecutors put the costs of repairs and maintenance to the cars allegedly offered by Temesan at the equivalent of $83,000. Temesan, who was sacked by a shareholders' meeting last March, faces up to 15 years in prison if convicted.
Temesan's lawyer Bogdan Ionescu said his client was innocent of all charges.
Police said they were also investigating allegations that Temesan had offered foreign exchange to more than 350 private companies at preferential rates.
Bancorex specialises in foreign trade financing and handles the bulk of foreign exchange trading on the local market. It is one of the most popular com mercial banks in Romania.
